notes: Written for an earlier 0.5*own + 0.5*mean(ancestors) weighting, where the parent goal's importance was strong enough to flip the across-group order despite task_low_1/2's higher own importance (0.7-0.8 vs 0.2-0.3) -- that flip was the fixture's whole point ('proves propagation changes the outcome, not just that it runs'). Revised down to 0.93*own + 0.07*mean(ancestors) (review on #474): 0.07 is too small for a 0.75-point ancestor-importance gap (goal_high=0.9 vs goal_low=0.15) to outweigh a 0.5-point own-importance gap (task_low ~0.75 vs task_high ~0.25) -- task_high_1=0.93*0.3+0.07*0.9=0.342, task_high_2=0.93*0.2+0.07*0.9=0.249, task_low_1=0.93*0.8+0.07*0.15=0.7545, task_low_2=0.93*0.7+0.07*0.15=0.6615. Own importance alone already produces this exact order; at this weight, this fixture no longer demonstrates that propagation changes the outcome -- it would rank the same with ancestors ignored entirely. Left as a regression check on the arithmetic (and on OWN_WEIGHT not silently drifting back up), not as evidence that hierarchy matters here.
